baselineDisplay.title: A Famous Monastery
baselineDisplay.question: What work were St. Bernard dogs famous for in the past?
baselineDisplay.questionZh: 圣伯纳德犬过去因从事什么工作而闻名？
baselineDisplay.text:
What work were St. Bernard dogs famous for in the past?

Editorial note: This reading corrects several historical claims; the seasonal scenes in its second half remain descriptions from the old textbook, and the recording retains the original wording. The Great St. Bernard Pass connects Switzerland to Italy.
At about 2,470 metres, it is a high mountain pass in the Alps.
The famous religious hospice of St. Bernard, founded in the eleventh century, stands at the Pass.
For generations, St. Bernard dogs helped to save travellers crossing the dangerous Pass.
Large dogs were kept at the hospice from the seventeenth century, first as guards and later to help travellers. The breed’s direct ancestors were local farm dogs.
A road tunnel later provided another route through the mountains. The Barry Foundation took over the kennel in 2005 and today also develops the dogs’ role in social support; the old account of routine snow rescues should be read in its historical setting.
The textbook warns that some people still attempt to cross the Pass on foot in dangerous conditions despite the tunnel.
In the old textbook’s summer scene, the monastery is very busy, for it is visited by thousands of people who cross the Pass in cars.
As there are so many people about, the dogs have to be kept in a special enclosure.
In winter, however, life at the monastery is quite different.
In this winter description, temperatures fall to about −30°C, and very few people attempt to cross the Pass.
The monks prefer winter to summer for they have more privacy.
The textbook also portrays the dogs wandering outside their enclosure in winter; this is not a description of their present seasonal arrangements.
The only regular visitors to the monastery in winter are parties of skiers who go there at Christmas and Easter.
These young people, who love the peace of the mountains, always receive a warm welcome at St. Bernard's monastery.

baselineDisplay.bodyTextZh:
编者注：本文校正了几处历史性论述；后半篇的季节场景仍属于旧教材描述，录音保留原文。大圣伯纳德山口连接瑞士与意大利。
它海拔约2,470米，是阿尔卑斯山中的一处高山山口。
著名的圣伯纳德宗教旅舍创立于十一世纪，就位于山口。
一代又一代圣伯纳德犬曾协助营救穿越险峻山口的旅行者。
从十七世纪起，旅舍便饲养大型犬，起初用于守卫，后来用于帮助旅行者。这个犬种的直接祖先是当地的农场犬。
后来建成的公路隧道提供了穿越山岭的另一条路线。巴里基金会于2005年接管犬舍，如今也发展这些犬在社会服务中的作用；旧课文关于日常雪地救援的描述应放在历史背景中理解。
教材提醒，尽管已有隧道，有些人仍会在危险条件下尝试徒步越过山口。
在旧教材描绘的夏季场景中，修道院十分繁忙，因为成千上万的人开车穿过山口前来参观。
由于周围人太多，这些狗必须被关在专门的围栏里。
然而，在冬天，修道院的生活却大不相同了。
在这段冬季描写中，气温降到约零下30摄氏度，尝试穿越山口的人很少。
僧侣们更喜欢冬天，因为那时他们更清静。
教材还描绘了犬只在冬天到围栏外自由活动的情景；这不是对其今日季节性饲养安排的描述。
冬天里，经常造访这座修道院的只有一批批滑雪者——他们会在圣诞节和复活节期间来到这里。
这些年轻人，他们热爱山间的宁静，在圣伯纳德修道院总是受到热情的欢迎。

display.title: A Famous Monastery
display.question: What are the St.Bernard dogs used for?
display.questionZh: 圣伯纳德犬是用来做什么的？
display.text:
What are the St.Bernard dogs used for?

The Great St.Bernard Pass connects Switzerland to Italy.
At 2,473 metres, it is one of the highest mountain passes in Europe.
The famous monastery of St.Bernard, which was founded in the eleventh century, lies about a mile away.
For hundreds of years, St.Bernard dogs have saved the lives of travellers crossing the dangerous Pass.
These friendly dogs, which were first brought from Asia, were used as watchdogs even in Roman times.
Now that a tunnel has been built through the mountains, the Pass is less dangerous, but each year, the dogs are still sent out into the snow whenever a traveller is in difficulty.
Despite the new tunnel, there are still a few people who rashly attempt to cross the Pass on foot.
During the summer months, the monastery is very busy, for it is visited by thousands of people who cross the Pass in cars.
As there are so many people about, the dogs have to be kept in a special enclosure.
In winter, however, life at the monastery is quite different.
The temperature drops to -30 degrees, and very few people attempt to cross the Pass.
The monks prefer winter to summer for they have more privacy.
The dogs have greater freedom, too, for they are allowed to wander outside their enclosure.
The only regular visitors to the monastery in winter are parties of skiers who go there at Christmas and Easter.
These young people, who love the peace of the mountains, always receive a warm welcome at St. Bernard's monastery.

display.bodyTextZh:
大圣伯纳德山口（Great St. Bernard Pass）将瑞士与意大利连接起来。
海拔2,473米，它是欧洲最高的山口。
著名的圣伯纳德修道院这座修道院建于十一世纪，坐落在约一英里外。
几个世纪以来，圣伯纳德犬一直拯救着那些穿越危险山口的旅行者的生命。
这些友好的狗狗最初是从亚洲引进的。甚至在罗马时代，它们就被用作看门狗。
既然已经修建了一条穿山隧道，山口的危险性就降低了，但每当有旅行者遇到困难时，这些狗仍会被派往雪地救援。
尽管有了这条新隧道，仍然有一些人贸然尝试徒步穿越这个山口。
在夏季，这座修道院非常繁忙。因为这里有成千上万的人开车穿过山口前来参观。
由于周围人太多，这些狗必须被关在专门的围栏里。
然而，在冬天，修道院的生活却大不相同了。
气温降到了零下30度。而且，很少有人试图穿越这个山口。
僧侣们更喜欢冬天，因为那时他们更清静。
这些狗也拥有更大的自由。因为它们被允许在围栏外四处走动。
冬天里，唯一经常造访这座修道院的人是一群滑雪者——他们会在圣诞节和复活节期间来到这里。
这些年轻人，他们热爱山间的宁静，在圣伯纳德修道院总是受到热情的欢迎。

著名的圣伯纳德修道院这座修道院建于十一世纪，坐落在约一英里外。
几个世纪以来，圣伯纳德犬一直拯救着那些穿越危险山口的旅行者的生命。
